mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -13.6% over the past four weeks with minimal week-on-week change. This plateau signals equilibrium in consumer avoidance behavior. Absent a shock to WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, retail mobility will remain flat or decline slightly over the next four weeks as the baseline of suppressed demand persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC change from t-3w to t-0w is only -1.8 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks without a corresponding rise in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered from -2.0% to +0.4% over four weeks, indicating restored confidence in essential-goods shopping. This confidence spillover will extend to discretionary retail within two weeks as consumers normalize shopping patterns across categories, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -2.0% at t-3w to +0.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM stabilizing above 0%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below -1% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain severely suppressed at -36.7%, indicating continued commuting collapse. This persistent transit deficit prevents the return of weekday retail clusters near transit hubs. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks as the absence of transit-dependent foot traffic compounds.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been between -35.0% and -36.7% for all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 percentage points over the next four weeks while TRANSIT remains below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility (-12.7%) and TRANSIT mobility (-36.7%) are both severely depressed and show no recovery trend. When both employment and transit access remain collapsed simultaneously, retail recovery is blocked because neither commuting-driven nor transit-dependent shopping can resume. RETAIL_REC will decline as this dual constraint persists.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -12% and -35% respectively for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show no recovery trajectory over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points over the next four weeks while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain in their current suppressed ranges.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed to -33.9% at t-0w, the lowest point in the four-week window. This sharp decline in outdoor recreation signals a shift toward indoor activities or increased restrictions. Within one week, this suppression will translate to compensatory indoor retail visits as consumers redirect leisure spending, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -30% in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-0w is -33.9%, down from -26.0% at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the first week following the PARKS collapse, or PARKS recovers above -20% without a corresponding RETAIL_REC rise.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained stable at +4.4% to +4.9% across all four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown or work-from-home regimes. Persistent home-based activity suppresses retail recovery because consumers remain confined. RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks as long as RESIDENTIAL elevation persists above +4%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +4% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been between +4.4% and +4.9% for all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points over the next four weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above +4%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovery (+0.4%) combined with stable RESIDENTIAL elevation (+4.9%) indicates consumers are shifting to home-based consumption and essential shopping only. This dual pattern suppresses discretionary retail. Over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC will decline as the home-centric consumption model persists despite grocery normalization.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above -1% AND RESIDENTIAL is above +4% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 percentage points over the next four weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains near 0% and RESIDENTIAL remains above +4%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has shown minimal deterioration from -13.0% to -12.7% over four weeks, suggesting employment activity is near a floor. If WORKPLACES stabilizes at this level without further decline over the next two weeks, it signals that workplace-based commuting has bottomed and will begin recovery, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks as commuting routines resume.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -12% for one week after remaining below -12.5% for two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has stabilized in the -12% to -13.4% range with minimal volatility
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not rise above -12% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not follow within the subsequent two weeks of WORKPLACES recovery.
